title: Picard group and first cohomology of units on ringed sites, naturally in pullback
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites chosen small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with sheaves of commutative unital rings $A,B$, respectively. A line module over either ring sheaf is a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] locally isomorphic to that ring sheaf. Write $\operatorname{Pic}(A)$ for the abelian group of isomorphism classes of line $A$-modules under sheaf tensor product, and $A^\times$ for the abelian sheaf $U\mapsto A(U)^\times$; similarly for $B$. Cohomology is the right derived functor of global sections of abelian sheaves. There is a canonical group isomorphism $c_A:\operatorname{Pic}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^1(\mathcal C,A^\times)$, sending a line $L$ to the class of its sheaf of generators $\underline{\operatorname{Isom}}_A(A,L)$. Here a $G$-torsor is a sheaf of sets with $G$-action, locally nonempty and with $G\times T\to T\times T$, $(g,t)\mapsto(gt,t)$, an isomorphism. For any morphism of ringed topoi $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),B)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),A)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], put $f^*L=B\otimes_{f^{-1}A}f^{-1}L$, where tensor is the sheafification of the presheaf of sectionwise tensor products, and let $\rho:f^{-1}A^\times\to B^\times$ be induced by the structural ring map. Then $f^*L$ is a line and $c_B([f^*L])=H^1(\rho)(f^*c_A([L]))$. Here $\Gamma(\mathcal C,F)=\operatorname{Hom}(*,F)$ for the final sheaf $*$, which is $F(e)$ when $\mathcal C$ has a final object $e$. The inner map $f^*:H^1(\mathcal C,A^\times)\to H^1(\mathcal D,f^{-1}A^\times)$ is defined by choosing injective resolutions $A^\times\to I^\bullet$ and $f^{-1}A^\times\to J^\bullet$ and a map of complexes $\beta:f^{-1}I^\bullet\to J^\bullet$ under $f^{-1}A^\times$ (it exists since $f^{-1}$ is exact), and taking $H^1$ of $\Gamma(\mathcal C,I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\eta}\Gamma(\mathcal C,f_*f^{-1}I^\bullet)=\Gamma(\mathcal D,f^{-1}I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\beta}\Gamma(\mathcal D,J^\bullet)$, where $\eta$ is the adjunction unit and $\Gamma(\mathcal C,f_*G)=\operatorname{Hom}(f^{-1}*,G)=\Gamma(\mathcal D,G)$ by adjunction, $f^{-1}$ preserving the final sheaf; it does not depend on the choices. No flatness assumption on $f^{-1}A\to B$ is required.

source.place: Tag 040E, lemma-h1-invertible, generator-torsor construction and its inverse; naturality follows from the same construction by extension of scalars (for line modules locally free of rank one, it works on any commutative ringed site).

proof.text: For a line $L$, let $T_L(U)$ be the isomorphisms $A|_U\to L|_U$. Compatible local isomorphisms glue: glue their values on $1$ as sections of $L$ and their inverses as maps into $A$; the two inverse identities hold after restriction, hence hold globally by the sheaf condition. Thus $T_L$ is a sheaf. It has local sections by the definition of a line. For two frames $t,t'$, $t^{-1}t'$ is multiplication by the unique unit $u=(t^{-1}t')(1)$, so $t'=ut$ with the action $(ut)(a)=t(ua)$. This proves simple transitivity and identifies $T_A$ with $A^\times$. Units themselves form a sheaf because compatible units and their inverses glue. Consequently $T_L$ is an $A^\times$-torsor.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: For an $A^\times$-torsor $T$, form the set presheaf $Q(U)=(T(U)\times A(U))/\sim$, where $(ut,a)\sim(t,ua)$, and let $M=Q^\#$ be its set sheafification. If $t\in T(U)$, then on every $V\to U$ a representative $[t',a]$ has a unique expression $[t,ua]$, with $t'=ut$. In this chart the quotient is $A|_U$. The local-section and local-equality properties of sheafification show the same for $M|_U$: represent a section locally by pairs, rewrite in the frame $t$, and glue their coefficients in $A$; equality of coefficients is checked after a covering. A change of frame $t'=ut$ changes coordinates by multiplication by $u$, an $A$-linear bijection. Define addition, zero, additive inverses and scalar multiplication in these coordinates. They agree on overlaps, so the sheaf condition glues them uniquely, and all module identities hold locally in $A$. Thus $M$ is a genuine line $A$-module. In particular no module structure is assigned to the possibly empty set $Q(U)$ before sheafification.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: The evaluation $[t,a]\mapsto t(a)$ defines a map $M(T_L)\to L$. On a chart with frame $t$ this is the isomorphism $a\mapsto t(a)$, so its local inverse gives a global inverse by uniqueness on overlaps. Conversely, $t\mapsto(a\mapsto[t,a])$ defines an equivariant map $T\to T_{M(T)}$. On a chart with section $t_0$ every frame is uniquely multiplication by a unit in the coordinate $M(T)\cong A$, so it has the unique preimage $ut_0$. These local inverses glue. Both constructions carry equivariant or module isomorphisms to isomorphisms by their displayed formulas, and hence induce inverse bijections on isomorphism classes.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: For lines $L,N$, the frame pair $(t,s)$ gives the frame of $L\otimes_A N$ sending $1$ to $t(1)\otimes s(1)$. The tensor is the sheafification of the sectionwise tensor. In frames its identification with $A$ is $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$, with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1$; these formulas are inverse by the tensor balancing relation. Replacing $(t,s)$ by $(ut,u^{-1}s)$ fixes the tensor frame. Thus the displayed map factors through the sheafified contracted product $T_L\wedge T_N$ and is a bijection locally, where it is multiplication of units modulo the antidiagonal action. Its local inverses glue. Apply the arbitrary-site torsor classification: $c_A([L])=\kappa_{A^\times}([T_L])$ is a bijection, carries tensor to addition, and carries $A$ to zero. For completeness the inverse line has sections locally given by the dual frame: the linear maps $L|_U\to A|_U$ glue as a sheaf, have dual coordinates under frame changes, and evaluation $L\otimes_A L^\vee\to A$ is locally multiplication and hence an isomorphism. This also verifies the group inverse in $\operatorname{Pic}(A)$. It is therefore the asserted canonical group isomorphism. The identical construction applies to $B$.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: For the given ringed-topos morphism, its underlying geometric inverse image is exact on abelian sheaves by the exactness node. The resolution-pullback node therefore applies with $F=A^\times$: its $P_f^1(F)$ is exactly the composite of unit, global-section adjunction and comparison $\beta$ written in the statement. It proves existence of $\beta$, choice independence, and compatibility with the connecting homomorphisms that will be used below. All global sections are $\operatorname{Hom}(*,-)$, so this application requires no final object of either site.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: Set $T=T_L$ and $V=f^{-1}T$. Its map to the final sheaf is locally surjective: apply preservation of locally surjective families to $T\to *$. Finite-limit preservation gives $(f^{-1}A^\times)\times V\cong V\times V$, hence $V$ is an $f^{-1}A^\times$-torsor. The universal evaluation trivialization $A\times T\cong L\times T$ pulls back to a trivialization of $f^{-1}L$ over the covering sheaf $V$. Here the transported module actions are the actions on underlying finite products. Extending scalars gives $B\otimes_{f^{-1}A}f^{-1}L\cong B$ locally over $V$: explicitly in the pulled frame $b\otimes a\mapsto b f^\sharp(a)$, with inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$. The balancing relation proves the inverse identities, also after sheafification. Local sections of $V$ exist after coverings of site objects, so $f^*L$ is a line on $\mathcal D$. Pulling back a frame and extending scalars gives a canonical map $s:V\to T_{f^*L}$ satisfying $s(uv)=\rho(u)s(v)$; this identity is the formula $1\otimes(ua)=f^\sharp(u)\otimes a$.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: Take the canonical extension $E_T$ in the torsor-classification node, and apply exact abelian inverse image. This gives $0\to f^{-1}A^\times\to f^{-1}E_T\to\mathbf Z_{\mathcal D}\to0$. The integer sheaf is preserved: internally it is the free abelian group on the final sheaf, and its free universal property is preserved by the induced abelian adjunction and finite products; equivalently the integer sheaf is the coproduct of copies of $*$ indexed by the integers. Indeed a map from that coproduct is a family of global sections indexed by the integers, and the sheafification adjunction identifies exactly the same data with a map from the sheafified constant integer presheaf. Apply left-adjoint preservation of small colimits and finite products to this coproduct and its addition, zero and inverse maps. Finite-limit preservation identifies the fibre over $1$ with $V=f^{-1}T$. Write $j:V\to f^{-1}E_T$ for the resulting inclusion of that fibre. The relation $j(uv)=j(v)+u$ is the inverse image of the original relation. The same classification node gives an extension $E_{T_{f^*L}}$ with generator inclusion $j'$.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: There is a morphism of the two extension sequences from the preceding step, with end maps $\rho$ and $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf Z}$. Construct its middle map locally as follows, using additive notation for both unit sheaves. On an object with $v\in V$, every section of the extension is uniquely $h+n j(v)$, where $h\in f^{-1}A^\times$ and $n$ is a section of the integer sheaf: subtract $n j(v)$ and use exactness at the kernel. Send it to $\rho(h)+n j'(s(v))$. If $v'=u+v$, then $j(v')=j(v)+u$ and $j'(s(v'))=j'(s(v))+\rho(u)$. Writing the same section using $v'$ replaces $h$ by $h-nu$; its proposed image is unchanged, since $\rho(h-nu)+n(j'(s(v))+\rho(u))=\rho(h)+n j'(s(v))$. These additive maps commute with restriction and agree on overlaps. Since $V$ is locally inhabited, they glue to the required map, restricting to $\rho$ on the kernel and preserving degree $n$.

source.place: Tag 040E (lemma-h1-invertible), generator-torsor and associated-module construction; Tag 03AJ (lemma-torsors-h1). The argument uses locally free rank one modules, so the local-ring hypothesis is unnecessary here.

proof.text: By compatibility of resolution pullback with boundaries, $f^*c_A([L])=P_f^1\delta_{E_T}(1)=\delta_{f^{-1}E_T}(1)$, since the degree-zero pullback sends $1$ to $1$. Naturality of connecting homomorphisms for the extension morphism just constructed yields $H^1(\rho)\delta_{f^{-1}E_T}(1)=\delta_{E_{T_{f^*L}}}(1)$. By the torsor-classification node and the definition of $c_B$, the right hand side is $c_B([f^*L])$. This is the required equation with the precise pullback map in the statement. All scalar extension calculations were on rank-one trivializations; none used flatness of $f^{-1}A\to B$.
